why: The canonical value-to-index map: for each nums[j], the partner it needs is target - nums[j], and a map of earlier values to their indices answers 'is the complement here, and where?' in O(1).
hints: For a fixed j, which single value would complete the pair? Can you find it without scanning?
Store value -> index for everything to the left of j. Look up target - nums[j] before inserting nums[j] itself, so an element is never paired with itself.
One pass: i = seen.get(target - x); if found return [i, j]; else seen[x] = j. The earlier index is found first, so the answer is already in ascending order. O(n).
pitfalls: Insert after the lookup, or [5] with target 10 would pair index 0 with itself.
Equal values at different indices are a valid pair ([5,5], target 10).
Return the indices, not the values; sorting the array would lose the original positions.
